name: Akira
summary: Akira is a prolific RaaS operation that ranked among the most active ransomware groups in 2025, reportedly extorting approximately $244M from 600+ victims. The group is notable for a rapid 'scan, steal, encrypt' lifecycle and for prioritizing backup infrastructure destruction early in intrusions to prevent victim recovery. In 2026 the group shifted away from experimental Rust code back to a faster, more stable C++ encryptor, reflecting a pragmatic tooling philosophy focused on operational efficiency.

ttps.notes: VPN appliances primary initial access; bypasses OTP-based MFA via inherited VPN config artifacts
Retained appliance secrets and compromised VPN credentials
C++ encryptor (reverted from Rust); hypervisor encryption to maximize infrastructure paralysis
Backup infrastructure targeted early to prevent recovery — VSS deletion, backup software disabling
Double extortion — data exfiltrated before encryption
SSH lateral movement observed in Linux/ESXi environments
Security tooling disabled early in intrusion lifecycle

detection_opportunities: Alert on VPN authentication from new devices or unusual geolocations
Detect VSS deletion and backup software termination commands
Monitor for ESXi and Hyper-V encryption activity
Alert on RClone or WinRAR usage in bulk data staging contexts
Detect AnyDesk installation outside of approved baseline
Monitor for rapid large-scale file modification events
